content: Alcon, a global medical company specializing in eye care products, is headquartered in Hünenberg, Switzerland, with its U.S. headquarters located in Fort Worth, Texas. Alcon was established in 1945 in Fort Worth, Texas, USA. The company began as a small pharmacy named after its founders, pharmacists Robert Alexander and William Conner. Alexander and Conner concentrated on developing sterile ophthalmic products, a niche that no other company was focusing on at the time. They built their business by researching and creating eye care products designed to minimize contamination and enhance safety. In 1947, Alcon was incorporated and experienced steady growth, eventually becoming a leader in the field of ophthalmology. In 1977, Nestlé, a Swiss multinational corporation, acquired Alcon. This acquisition marked Nestlé's first foray into the pharmaceutical industry during a period of rapid expansion for the company. Under Nestlé's ownership, Alcon expanded its manufacturing capabilities by establishing new facilities in South America and Europe and significantly increasing its investment in research and development. During the 1980s and 1990s, Alcon continued its growth trajectory, becoming the largest and most profitable ophthalmic company globally. The company broadened its product portfolio, moving beyond pharmaceuticals to include surgical products. Notably, the AcrySof intraocular lens implant became the most widely used implant in cataract surgeries worldwide. Today, Alcon operates in 75 countries, and its products are sold in over 180 countries. The company employs more than 12,000 individuals globally. In 2002, Alcon was spun off from Nestlé and re-entered the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) with an initial public offering (IPO) on March 21. Despite the spin-off, Nestlé retained 75% of Alcon's stock.
